narrationSegments.text: A Xiangqi board has nine vertical files and ten horizontal ranks, creating ninety intersections.
narrationSegments.headline: Nine Files, Ten Ranks
narrationSegments.visualInstruction: Draw all nine vertical files and ten horizontal ranks in sequence, then pulse the 90 legal intersections.

narrationSegments.text: The pieces stand on those intersections, and a move travels along the lines between them.
narrationSegments.headline: Points And Paths
narrationSegments.visualInstruction: Select one real red pawn on an intersection, pulse its origin, and show its legal destination points along the board lines.

narrationSegments.text: The horizontal river divides the two sides, while the central files connect the battlefield from one palace to the other.
narrationSegments.headline: River And Palaces
narrationSegments.visualInstruction: Shade the river band, outline both central 3-by-3 palaces with their X diagonals, and brighten the three central files.

narrationSegments.text: A chariot values an open file, a cannon values a line with the right screen, and a horse needs an unobstructed leg.
narrationSegments.headline: Three Movement Constraints
narrationSegments.visualInstruction: Show three short legal demonstrations: a chariot ray on an open file, a cannon with exactly one screen, and a horse with its leg clear versus blocked.
